hooks.text: The most famous cow in history never kicked that lantern.
In October 1871, a raging inferno destroyed the city of Chicago.
Who really burned down the entire city of Chicago in 1871?

title: Why Chicago Took 126 Years to Clear O'Leary's Cow 😳
description: The Great Chicago Fire of 1871 was blamed on Mrs. O'Leary's cow, but the real story was a complete fabrication.

beats.text: The most famous cow in history never kicked that lantern.
beats.visual: Nineteenth-century illustration of a cow knocking over a lantern, 1871

beats.text: On October 8, 1871, a devastating fire broke out on DeKoven Street.
beats.visual: Lithograph depicting the Great Chicago Fire in full blaze, 1871
queries: John R. Chapin Chicago fire engraving

beats.text: Fueled by severe drought, the Great Chicago Fire killed about 300 people.
beats.visual: Photograph of ruins of the Cook County Courthouse after the fire, 1871

beats.text: Seeking a scapegoat, journalist Michael Ahern blamed Irish immigrant Catherine O’Leary.
beats.visual: Photograph of Catherine O'Leary, nineteenth century

beats.text: He claimed her cow kicked a lantern, but O’Leary was asleep in bed.
beats.visual: Photograph of the O'Leary family cottage surviving the fire, 1871

beats.text: Ahern later admitted he fabricated the entire story for a colorful headline.
beats.visual: Newspaper illustration of refugees escaping the Great Chicago Fire, 1871
queries: Great Chicago Fire refugees lakefront illustration

beats.text: Chicago took 126 years to officially clear her name.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Chicago Fire Academy built on the O'Leary barn site, 2021
